updates.sentence:
5 years federal prison + $10,000 fine

Charges as recorded: False statement (18 U.S.C. § 1001) in non-Communist affidavit under Taft-Hartley §9(h). Affirmed Bryson v. United States, 396 U.S. 64 (1969).

Custody chronology: The Supreme Court reported that Bryson served almost two years before parole in December 1959 (Bryson v. United States, 396 U.S. 64, footnote 4). His parole continued while part of the fine remained unpaid; parole was not continued imprisonment. The National Guardian of June 27, 1955 reported his release after the appeals court reduced bail on June 17. The exact admission date for the later prison term and exact December parole day remain unverified.
